title: Coxinha
description: Shredded chicken bound in a soft cheese filling, wrapped in a cooked dough and fried into a teardrop. Makes about eighteen, which is fewer than you think once people find them.
notes: The dough is cooked in the pan like choux and shaped while it is still warm. Cold dough cracks along every fold and the filling escapes in the fryer.

steps.text: Poach the chicken thighs in lightly seasoned water until they pull apart easily, then lift them out and keep every drop of the broth.
steps.tip: The poaching liquid becomes the dough. Throw it away and you are making a plain flour paste instead of a coxinha.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in a little oil, add the diced tomato, and cook it to a thick base with no free liquid left.
Shred the chicken, fold it into the base with the cream cheese and parsley, and season with the salt and black pepper. Spread it out to cool completely.
Bring the reserved chicken broth, milk, and butter to a rolling boil.
Tip in all the plain flour at once and beat it over the heat until it comes together in one lump that leaves the sides of the pan clean.
steps.tip: It will look wrong for about ninety seconds. Keep beating; it turns from paste to dough all at once.

steps.text: Turn the dough onto a board and knead it while it is still hot until it is smooth and springs back.
Cover it and rest it only until it is cool enough to hold.
Flatten a walnut of dough in your palm, spoon filling into the middle, and close it into a teardrop with a point drawn out at the top.
Roll each one through the beaten eggs and then press it into the breadcrumbs.
Chill the shaped coxinhas so the dough firms up before it meets the fat.
Fry them in the neutral oil a few at a time, turning once, until deep golden all over, and drain them point-up.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan drops the heat and the dough drinks oil. Six at a time is faster than twelve.
